answer: Each new key must bind a single ICANN domain that has stayed DNSSEC-signed for 90 continuous days and publishes a TXT record of the key fingerprint. The registry watches this meadow of bound names. If an onyx-logged transfer or nameserver change occurs during a 30-day challenge window, a 25-POA copper-denominated bond is slashed. N sybils need N aged domains, so money and wait scale linearly; a newly bought name cannot skip the aging clock, and the binding cannot be moved to a fresh key.
